episode_title: The 6 Unit Economics VCs Use to Evaluate Startups | Paige Soya, Nick Duafala & K Street Capital

real_qa.q: What is the ideal LTV to CAC ratio that K Street Capital looks for in SaaS businesses?
real_qa.r: K Street Capital looks for an LTV to CAC ratio between 3x to 5x as a baseline, with ratios greater than 5x showing that a customer is worth a lot and acquisition costs are low, which is a really great indicator. The team has some businesses with ratios as high as 20x. However, if a business is trending in the right direction even below 3x, that is weighted more heavily in their evaluation.
real_qa.requete: LTV CAC ratio SaaS K Street Capital

real_qa.q: What gross margin range does K Street Capital target for SaaS businesses?
real_qa.r: For SaaS businesses, K Street Capital targets gross margins between 70 and 90 percent. If a company has lower margins like 65 percent but is trending upward, that is preferable to a business with 80 percent margins that are trending down. However, at the early stage these metrics might be depressed because companies are adding AWS and hosting costs without having enough revenue yet.

real_qa.q: What is the acceptable payback period threshold for customer acquisition costs according to K Street Capital?
real_qa.r: K Street Capital considers under 18 months to be a pretty good payback period. If the payback period goes higher than 24 months, they start having concerns because it can put a drag on the business. Under 12 months is really good, and they have invested in a founder CEO whose payback period was 3 months, which was amazing.
real_qa.requete: customer acquisition payback period 18 months 24 months

real_qa.q: What Net Revenue Retention and Gross Revenue Retention thresholds indicate a healthy SaaS business?
real_qa.r: For Net Revenue Retention, anything above 100 percent indicates consistent business growth. For Gross Revenue Retention, 85 percent is considered healthy, and anything below 80 percent signals a retention problem. If monthly churn is less than 1 percent, that is acceptable, but losing more than 5 percent per month is a serious problem.
real_qa.requete: NRR GRR retention 85 percent 90 percent churn

real_qa.q: What is burn multiple and how is it calculated in venture capital due diligence?
real_qa.r: Burn multiple is your net burn divided by your net new ARR. For example, if a company is burning 100K per month and bringing in 100K of new ARR that month, the burn multiple is one. It is a metric that has become more or less popular depending on market conditions, but K Street Capital always looks at it to ensure the business model makes sense.
real_qa.requete: burn multiple net burn ARR venture capital
